items.title: Beta-sets, the shift, and the e-runner abacus of a partition
items.statement:
Let $\lambda\vdash n$ be a partition with English Young diagram $[\lambda]$, parts
$\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_m>0$ and conjugate $\lambda'$
([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). For $1\le i\le m$ put
$$b_i(\lambda):=\lambda_i+m-i=h_{i,1}(\lambda),$$
the hook length of the first node of row $i$
([[def-hook-arm-leg-and-hook-length]]); since
$h_{i,1}(\lambda)=\lambda_i+\lambda'_1-i$ and $m=\lambda'_1$, the two expressions
agree. Then
$$X_\lambda:=\{b_1(\lambda)>b_2(\lambda)>\cdots>b_m(\lambda)\}$$
is the set of **first-column hook lengths** of $\lambda$, a finite strictly
decreasing set of positive integers.

A **$\beta$-set** is a finite set $X=\{h_1>\cdots>h_m\}\subseteq\mathbb N_0$ of
nonnegative integers, written in strictly decreasing order. For $l\in\mathbb N_0$
the **$l$-shift** of $X$ is
$$X+l:=\{h+l:h\in X\}\cup\{l-1,l-2,\dots,1,0\}$$
(for $l=0$ this is $X$ itself, the second set being empty), and the **partition
of $X$** is
$$P(X):=(h_1-(m-1),\,h_2-(m-2),\,\dots,\,h_m-0),$$
with trailing zeros deleted; this is a weakly decreasing sequence of
nonnegative integers ending in $h_m$, hence a partition of
$\sum_i h_i-m(m-1)/2$ after deleting its zeros. A $\beta$-set **for** $\lambda$
is a $\beta$-set $X$ with $P(X)=\lambda$.

Let $e\ge2$. **James's $e$-abacus** has $e$ runners $0,1,\dots,e-1$ drawn left to
right, with rows labelled $a=0,1,2,\dots$ downward; the position in row $a$ of
runner $i$ carries the label $ae+i$. An **$e$-abacus configuration** $A$ is a
finite set of **beads** placed in distinct positions of this abacus; a position
without a bead is a **gap**. The configuration $A_X$ of a $\beta$-set $X$ carries
a bead in the positions of $X$, and conversely $X_A$ is the set of position
labels of the beads of $A$; the two constructions are mutually inverse, so they
biject finite $\beta$-sets with finite bead configurations. Finally
$P(A):=P(X_A)$, and $A_\lambda:=A_{X_\lambda}$.
items.strategy: The beta inverse is h_i=lambda_i+m-i with padded zeros. Strictly decreasing nonnegative labels give weakly decreasing nonnegative parts. Every representation has m>=ell(lambda) and the unique shift m-ell(lambda), and Euclidean division gives the bead inverse. Empty beta sets, zero labels, empty partition, l=0 and empty runners are valid. No AC. Read the partition/hook definitions and current beta definition; no finding and no decision owed.

items.title: Hooks are bead-gap pairs on the abacus
items.statement:
Let $e\ge2$, let $\lambda\vdash n$ and let $X=\{h_1>h_2>\cdots>h_m\}$ be a
$\beta$-set for $\lambda$, so that $P(X)=\lambda$
([[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]]). Write $H_i(\lambda)$ for
the set of hook lengths in row $i$ of $[\lambda]$: thus $h\in H_i(\lambda)$
means $h=h_{i,j}(\lambda)$ for some node $(i,j)\in[\lambda]$, and
$H_i(\lambda)=\emptyset$ for $i>\ell(\lambda)$
([[def-hook-arm-leg-and-hook-length]]).

(i) For every $h\ge0$ and every $i\in[m]$, $h\in H_i(\lambda)$ if and only if
$h\le h_i$ and $h_i-h\notin X$. Equivalently, the hooks of $\lambda$
correspond bijectively to the **bead-gap pairs** $(b,g)$ with $b\in X$,
$g\notin X$ and $0\le g<b$; the hook $H_{i,j}(\lambda)$ corresponds to
$$(b,g)=\bigl(h_i,\;h_i-h_{i,j}(\lambda)\bigr),$$
and then $|H_{i,j}(\lambda)|=b-g$.

(ii) Fix a node $(i,j)\in[\lambda]$ and let $(b,g)$ be its bead-gap pair as in
(i). Then
$$X':=(X\setminus\{b\})\cup\{g\}$$
is again a $\beta$-set, now for the partition $\lambda\setminus R_{i,j}$
obtained from $\lambda$ by removing the removable border strip $R_{i,j}$ that
corresponds to the hook of $(i,j)$, of size $h_{i,j}(\lambda)$ and height
$\ell(i,j)=\lambda'_j-i$
([[def-removable-border-strip-and-height]],
[[lem-hooks-correspond-to-removable-border-strips]]); in terms of parts, with
$b_0:=\ell(i,j)=\lambda'_j-i$,
$$\lambda\setminus R_{i,j}=\bigl(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{i-1},\,\lambda_{i+1}-1,\dots,\lambda_{i+b_0}-1,\,j-1,\,\lambda_{i+b_0+1},\dots\bigr),$$
so that $|\lambda\setminus R_{i,j}|=n-h_{i,j}(\lambda)$. Finally $X'$ is
obtained from the configuration $A_X$ by moving the bead from position $b$ to
the gap $g$.

(iii) In particular $e\mid h_{i,j}(\lambda)$ if and only if $b\equiv g\pmod e$,
that is, if and only if the bead $b$ and the gap $g$ lie on the same runner of
the $e$-abacus; then $g=b-e\cdot(h_{i,j}(\lambda)/e)$ and the move in (ii) is
the slide of the bead $b$ up $h_{i,j}(\lambda)/e$ rows on its own runner. A
hook of length $e$ in row $i$ of $\lambda$ exists if and only if $h_i\ge e$
and $h_i-e\notin X$; Thus $\lambda$ has a hook of length $e$ if and only if some bead of $X$ has a gap
in the position $e$ labels above it on its own runner.

No choice principle is used.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An integer $e\ge2$, a partition $\lambda\vdash n$ with $t:=\ell(\lambda)$ parts, and a $\beta$-set $X=\{h_1>\cdots>h_m\}$ for $\lambda$, so that $P(X)=\lambda$ ([[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]]).

[F1] Hook lengths: $h_{i,j}(\lambda)=\lambda_i-j+\lambda'_j-i+1$ for $(i,j)\in[\lambda]$, and for fixed $i$ the map $j\mapsto h_{i,j}(\lambda)$ is strictly decreasing on $1\le j\le\lambda_i$, because $h_{i,j}(\lambda)-h_{i,j+1}(\lambda)=1+\lambda'_j-\lambda'_{j+1}\ge1$; hence the hook lengths in a fixed row are pairwise distinct and $h_{i,j}(\lambda)\ge1$ ([[def-hook-arm-leg-and-hook-length]]).

[F2] For a $\beta$-set $Y=\{y_1>\cdots>y_r\}$ one has $P(Y)_j=y_j-(r-j)$ for $1\le j\le r$, after which trailing zeros are deleted: indeed there are $y_j$ positions $0,1,\dots,y_j-1$ below the bead $y_j$, of which exactly $r-j$ are occupied by the beads $y_{j+1},\dots,y_r$, so $y_j-(r-j)$ of them are gaps, and the definition of $P$ takes exactly this difference ([[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]]).

[F3] The $\beta$-sets of $\lambda$ are exactly the sets $X_\lambda+l$, $l\in\mathbb N_0$, where $X_\lambda=\{b_1(\lambda)>\cdots>b_t(\lambda)\}$ with $b_i(\lambda)=h_{i,1}(\lambda)=\lambda_i+t-i$, and $|X_\lambda+l|=t+l$ ([[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]]).

[F4] A removable border strip of $\lambda$ is a nonempty edge-connected set of nodes containing no $2\times2$ block whose complement in $[\lambda]$ is again a Young diagram; its height is its number of occupied rows minus one, and for a strip that is the hook of a node it equals the leg length of that node ([[def-removable-border-strip-and-height]], [[lem-hooks-correspond-to-removable-border-strips]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Pad $\lambda$ with zeros to length $m$. By [F3], $h_i=\lambda_i+m-i$. Below $h_i$ there are exactly $m-i$ beads, hence $h_i-(m-i)=\lambda_i$ gaps. For a node $(i,j)$ put $g_j=h_i-h_{i,j}(\lambda)=m+j-1-\lambda'_j$. These values are distinct by [F1], satisfy $0\le g_j<h_i$, and are gaps: equality $g_j=h_x=\lambda_x+m-x$ would give $\lambda_x-j+\lambda'_j-x+1=0$. If $x\le\lambda'_j$, both differences are nonnegative; otherwise both are at most $-1$, since $\lambda_x<j$. Neither case gives zero. Thus the $\lambda_i$ numbers $g_j$ exhaust the gaps below $h_i$, including the empty set when $\lambda_i=0$. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 Fix $(i,j)$ and put $r=\lambda'_j$ and $g=m+j-1-r$. The rim strip of [F4] has complement with rows $\mu_p=\lambda_p$ outside $i\le p\le r$, $\mu_p=\lambda_{p+1}-1$ for $i\le p<r$, and $\mu_r=j-1$: in row $p$ the strip occupies the rim nodes with column at least $j$, whose complement ends at $\max(j-1,\lambda_{p+1}-1)$. For $p<r$ one has $\lambda_{p+1}\ge j$, while $\lambda_{r+1}<j$. These formulas give the displayed partition in (ii), with trailing zeros deleted, and its size is $n-h_{i,j}(\lambda)$. [F1, F4, construct, algebra]

2.1 Consequently, for $h\ge0$, $h\in H_i(\lambda)$ exactly when $h\le h_i$ and $h_i-h\notin X$: at $h=0$ the latter fails because $h_i\in X$, and for $h>h_i$ its first inequality fails. For $1\le h\le h_i$ this is the gap correspondence in step 1.1. The bead $h_i$ determines $i$, and the distinct row hook lengths determine $j$, so $(i,j)\mapsto(h_i,g_j)$ is the asserted bijection with length $h_i-g_j$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 The new value $g$ is below $h_r$ because $h_r-g=\lambda_r-j+1\ge1$, and, if $r<m$, above $h_{r+1}$ because $g-h_{r+1}=j-\lambda_{r+1}\ge1$. Hence the decreasing list of $X'=(X\setminus\{h_i\})\cup\{g\}$ is $h_1,\ldots,h_{i-1},h_{i+1},\ldots,h_r,g,h_{r+1},\ldots,h_m$. Applying [F2] gives precisely the parts $\mu_p$ in step 1.2. Thus $P(X')=\lambda\setminus R_{i,j}$, and the abacus change is the relocation of the bead $h_i$ to $g$. [F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 The length is $b-g$, so $e\mid h_{i,j}(\lambda)$ exactly when $b\equiv g\pmod e$. In that case the bead remains on its runner, moves up $h_{i,j}(\lambda)/e$ rows, and all runner bead counts are unchanged. Without this divisibility assumption the relocation may change runners. In row $i$ a hook of length $e$ exists exactly when $h_i\ge e$ and $h_i-e\notin X$, by step 2.1; existential quantification over $i$ gives the final bead criterion in (iii). [step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: The e-core, the e-quotient, and the e-weight
items.statement:
Let $e\ge2$, let $\lambda\vdash n$ and let
$X=\{h_1>h_2>\cdots>h_m\}$ be a $\beta$-set for $\lambda$, with first-column
hook lengths $b_i(\lambda)$ and $e$-abacus configuration $A_X$ as in
[[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]]; hooks and their lengths
are those of [[def-hook-arm-leg-and-hook-length]], and the hook/bead-gap
dictionary is [[lem-hooks-are-bead-gap-pairs-on-an-abacus]].

**$e$-core partition.** The partition $\lambda$ is an **$e$-core** when
$e\notin H(\lambda)$, that is, when no hook of $\lambda$ has length $e$; by
[[lem-hooks-are-bead-gap-pairs-on-an-abacus]](iii) this is the case exactly
when no bead of $A_X$ has a gap in the position $e$ labels above it on its own
runner. The empty partition is an $e$-core, and so is every $\lambda$ with
$|\lambda|<e$.

**Runner label sets.** For $i\in\{0,1,\dots,e-1\}$ let
$$X^{(e)}_i:=\{a\in\mathbb N_0:ae+i\in X\}$$
be the set of row labels of the beads of $A_X$ on runner $i$. The $X^{(e)}_i$
are finite subsets of $\mathbb N_0$ and may overlap. The disjoint union
$\bigsqcup_i\{i\}\times X^{(e)}_i$ records each bead with its runner and row;
the map $(i,a)\mapsto ae+i$ bijects it with $X$.

**$e$-core.** The **top-packed $\beta$-set** of $X$ is
$$X^{(e)}:=\bigcup_{i=0}^{e-1}\{ae+i:0\le a\le|X^{(e)}_i|-1\},$$
the configuration obtained from $A_X$ by sliding every bead up as far as it
goes on its own runner, i.e. into the topmost $|X^{(e)}_i|$ positions of
runner $i$. The **$e$-core** of $\lambda$ is
$$C_e(\lambda):=P(X^{(e)}).$$

**$e$-quotient and $e$-weight.** Choose the $\beta$-set $X$ of $\lambda$ to be
*normalised*, meaning $|X|\equiv0\pmod e$. Then define the **$e$-quotient** of
$\lambda$ to be the $e$-tuple of partitions
$$Q_e(\lambda):=(\lambda^{(0)},\lambda^{(1)},\dots,\lambda^{(e-1)}),\qquad \lambda^{(i)}:=P(X^{(e)}_i),$$
each runner read as a $1$-abacus, and the **$e$-weight** of $\lambda$ to be
$$w_e(\lambda):=|Q_e(\lambda)|:=\textstyle\sum_{i=0}^{e-1}|\lambda^{(i)}|.$$
A normalised $\beta$-set exists: by
[[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]] the $\beta$-sets of
$\lambda$ are the sets $X_\lambda+l$, $l\in\mathbb N_0$, and
$|X_\lambda+l|=|X_\lambda|+l$, so among the $e$ consecutive shifts
$l,\dots,l+e-1$ exactly one has size divisible by $e$.

No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Runner row sets can overlap; their tagged disjoint union, not an untagged union, bijects X. The one-shift counts are (c_(e-1)+1,c_0,...), and the e-shift adds a zero bead on each runner and shifts existing rows by 1, preserving component partitions. Normalized lengths differ by multiples of e. The regularity proof correctly uses the bottom e rows of the same length a; transposition exchanges arm and leg. Empty runners and the empty partition are covered, no AC. The definition defers core/ordered-quotient invariance to its proved_here justified_by theorem, checked next in dependency order. Compared the exact pre-reader bytes; current corrections are sound.

items.title: Virtual Weyl combinations detect q-Schur block separation
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^{\times}$, $d,n\ge1$, and let $S=S(d,n)$ be the
$q$-Schur algebra over $F$ with Weyl modules $W^{\lambda}$ for
$\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n)$
([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). Let $M$ be a finite
dimensional right $S$-module all of whose composition factors lie in a single
block $B$ of $S$
([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]),
and let integers $a_{\lambda}$, $\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n)$, satisfy
$$[M]=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n)}a_{\lambda}[W^{\lambda}]$$
in the Grothendieck group $G_0(S\text{-mod})$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]]). Then
$W^{\lambda}$ lies in $B$ whenever $a_{\lambda}\ne0$. In particular no nonzero
virtual combination of Weyl classes all of whose terms lie outside $B$ can
equal the class of a module in $B$.

No choice principle is used.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A field $F$, $q\in F^{\times}$, $d,n\ge1$, the algebra $S=S(d,n)$ with Weyl modules $W^{\lambda}$, $\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n)$, a finite dimensional right $S$-module $M$ whose composition factors all lie in one block $B$, and integers $a_{\lambda}$ with $[M]=\sum_{\lambda}a_{\lambda}[W^{\lambda}]$ in $G_0(S\text{-mod})$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]], [[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]]).

[F1] Blocks: $1=\sum_i\epsilon_i$ is the unique decomposition of the identity of $S$ into pairwise orthogonal primitive central idempotents, the blocks are the two-sided ideals $B_i=S\epsilon_i=\epsilon_iS$, and for every right $S$-module $N$ one has $N=\bigoplus_iN\epsilon_i$; a simple module $L$ lies in exactly one block and satisfies $L\epsilon_i=L$ for that $i$ ([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]). We write $\epsilon_B$ for the idempotent of the block $B$ of the statement.

[F2] Each Weyl module has nonzero simple head $L^\lambda$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]).

[F3] The proof of [[lem-semistandard-weight-dimensions-detect-virtual-weyl-classes]], steps 1.1 and 3.1, gives additive weight dimensions and the weight matrix $K_{\lambda\nu}=\dim(W^\lambda1_\nu)$. This matrix, restricted to partitions with at most $d$ parts, is unitriangular and hence invertible by [[lem-kostka-change-of-basis-is-dominance-unitriangular]]. Applying these dimensions to a zero virtual Weyl combination forces every coefficient to vanish. This proves the linear independence used here; no Weyl filtration of an arbitrary module is assumed.

[F4] An exact functor between abelian categories induces a homomorphism of Grothendieck groups, and the finite-dimensional $S$-modules form an abelian category in which $G_0$ is computed by composition multiplicities ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Multiplication by the central idempotent $\epsilon_B$ is the projection of every right $S$-module onto its $B$-summand: $N=\bigoplus_iN\epsilon_i$ by [F1], so $N\epsilon_B$ is that direct summand and is a submodule, and $N\epsilon_B=N$ exactly when all composition factors of $N$ lie in $B$. The assignment $N\mapsto N\epsilon_B$ is exact, because it is the projection onto a direct summand of the identity functor: for $f:N\to N'$ one has $f(N\epsilon_B)=f(N)\epsilon_B$, $\ker(f|_{N\epsilon_B})=(\ker f)\epsilon_B$ and $\operatorname{im}(f|_{N\epsilon_B})=(\operatorname{im}f)\epsilon_B$, so it preserves kernels and images. [F1, F4]

1.2 A nonzero finite-dimensional module has a simple quotient: choose a proper submodule of maximal vector-space dimension. If a Weyl module had two nonzero summands, each would have a nonzero head, so its head would not be simple, contrary to [F2]. Thus it is indecomposable. Its block decomposition [F1] has precisely one nonzero summand, the block containing its head $L^\lambda$; hence $W^\lambda\epsilon_B$ is either $W^\lambda$ or $0$. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Apply the exact projection of step 1.1 to the class identity of the hypothesis. Since $M\epsilon_B=M$ by the hypothesis that all composition factors of $M$ lie in $B$, and since $W^{\lambda}\epsilon_B$ is $W^{\lambda}$ or $0$ by step 1.2, the induced identity in $G_0$ reads $$[M]=\sum_{\lambda:\,W^{\lambda}\in B}a_{\lambda}[W^{\lambda}].$$ Subtracting it from the given identity $[M]=\sum_{\lambda}a_{\lambda}[W^{\lambda}]$ yields $$\sum_{\lambda:\,W^{\lambda}\notin B}a_{\lambda}[W^{\lambda}]=0$$ in $G_0(S\text{-mod})$. [F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 By the linear independence of the Weyl classes [F3], all coefficients in the vanishing combination of step 2.1 are zero: $a_{\lambda}=0$ for every $\lambda$ with $W^{\lambda}\notin B$, which is the contrapositive of the assertion that $a_{\lambda}\ne0$ implies $W^{\lambda}\in B$. [F3, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: The e-core is independent of the rim hook removal order
items.statement:
Let $e\ge2$ and let $\lambda\vdash n$ with $e$-abacus configurations as in
[[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]] and the top-packed set
$X^{(e)}$ of [[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]. For every $\beta$-set $X$
of $\lambda$ the partition $P(X^{(e)})$ is the same, so the $e$-core
$C_e(\lambda)=P(X^{(e)})$ is a well-defined $e$-core partition, and it is
exactly the terminal partition reached by successively removing removable
border strips of size $e$ from $[\lambda]$ until none is left
([[def-removable-border-strip-and-height]],
[[lem-hooks-correspond-to-removable-border-strips]]). In particular every
maximal sequence of such removals gives the same terminal partition
$C_e(\lambda)$, each removed strip has size exactly $e$, and the terminal
partition contains no hook of length $e$. Moreover any two normalised beta-sets
($e\mid|X|$) give the same ordered quotient $Q_e(\lambda)$ and weight.

No choice principle is used.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An integer $e\ge2$, a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, and a $\beta$-set $X$ of $\lambda$ with runner label sets $X^{(e)}_i$, counts $c_i:=|X^{(e)}_i|$ and top-packed set $X^{(e)}$ as in [[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]].

[F1] Hooks correspond to bead-gap pairs $(b,g)$ with length $b-g$; deleting the corresponding rim strip replaces $b$ by $g$. If the length is divisible by $e$, the relocation stays on the same runner ([[lem-hooks-are-bead-gap-pairs-on-an-abacus]]).

[F2] The top-packed set has runner $i$ occupied in rows $0,\ldots,c_i-1$, and $C_e(\lambda)=P(X^{(e)})$. The ordered quotient is computed from the partitions of the runner row-label sets of a normalised beta-set ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]).

[F3] Every beta-set of $\lambda$ is $X_\lambda+l$ for a unique $l\ge0$, and $P(X+l)=P(X)$. Thus, after interchanging two beta-sets if necessary, the larger one is a shift of the smaller one ([[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]]).

[F4] The hook/rim-strip correspondence is a bijection preserving size ([[def-removable-border-strip-and-height]], [[lem-hooks-correspond-to-removable-border-strips]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Fix a $\beta$-set $X$ of a partition $\mu$ and write its elements as $h_1>\cdots>h_m$. By [F1] the hooks of length $e$ of $\mu$ correspond bijectively to the beads $b=h_i$ with $h_i\ge e$ and $h_i-e\notin X$, the correspondence sending such a bead to the rim strip $R_{i,j}(\mu)$ attached to the node with $h_{i,j}(\mu)=e$, and removal of that strip replaces $X$ by $X'=(X\setminus\{h_i\})\cup\{h_i-e\}$, a $\beta$-set for $\mu\setminus R_{i,j}(\mu)$ of the same size $m$. In particular $\mu$ has no hook of length $e$ exactly when no bead of $X$ has a gap in the position $e$ labels above it on its own runner. [F1, F2]

1.2 Compute the shift directly. For $Y=X+1$, its runner sets are $Y^{(e)}_0=(X^{(e)}_{e-1})+1$ and $Y^{(e)}_i=X^{(e)}_{i-1}$ for $1\le i<e$: the last runner wraps to runner $0$ one row lower, and the shift adds the bead at $0$. Its counts are $(c_{e-1}+1,c_0,\ldots,c_{e-2})$. Packing with these counts gives $Y^{(e)}=(X^{(e)})+1$, so $P(Y^{(e)})=P(X^{(e)})$ by [F3]. Iteration proves core independence for all beta-sets of $\lambda$. After $e$ shifts, every runner row-label set has undergone one beta-set shift by $1$, so its partition is unchanged. Normalised beta-sets differ by a multiple of $e$, proving independence of the ordered quotient and its total size. [F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Call a bead of $X$ *movable* when the position $e$ labels above it on its runner is a gap, so that by step 1.1 the movable beads are exactly the hooks of length $e$ of $\mu$; moving a bead up one row replaces $X$ by a $\beta$-set of $\mu$ minus that hook, and the counts $|X^{(e)}_i|$ of beads on each runner are unchanged. A configuration is top-packed precisely when it has no movable bead: a top-packed runner carries beads in the rows $0,1,\dots,c_i-1$, so the row above a bead is a bead again (and row $0$ has no row above it), while if some runner is not top-packed there are a gap in row $g$ and a bead in a row $a>g$ on that runner; choosing $a$ minimal among the bead rows larger than $g$, the row $a-1$ is a gap, so the bead in row $a$ is movable. [F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Every sequence of moves of steps 1.1 and 2.1 is finite: the quantity $\Phi:=\sum_{i}\sum_{a\in X^{(e)}_i}a$ is the total of the row labels of all beads, and each move replaces a bead's row label $a$ by $a-1$, so $\Phi$ decreases by exactly $1$ and is a nonnegative integer. A sequence is maximal exactly when it stops at a configuration with no movable bead, that is, by step 2.1, exactly when it stops at the top-packed configuration of the counts $(c_i)$; and that configuration is unique, since a runner with $c_i$ beads has exactly one top-packed state, the rows $0,\dots,c_i-1$. Hence every maximal sequence of moves starting from $X$ ends at the same configuration, namely $X^{(e)}$, and therefore at the same terminal partition $P(X^{(e)})$. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 By step 1.2 the partition $P(X^{(e)})$ does not depend on the chosen $\beta$-set $X$, so $C_e(\lambda):=P(X^{(e)})$ is well-defined; by step 3.1 it is the common terminal partition of all maximal sequences of e-hook removals, and by step 2.1 a terminal configuration is top-packed, hence carries no movable bead, hence its partition has no hook of length $e$ by step 1.1; thus $C_e(\lambda)$ is an $e$-core. Every strip removed along such a sequence corresponds to a node hook of length exactly $e$ and so has size $e$ by [F4]. This proves all the asserted properties. [F2, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 1.2] ∎

items.title: The e-quotient controls the hooks of e-divisible length
items.statement:
Let $e\ge2$ and let $\lambda\vdash n$ with $e$-quotient
$Q_e(\lambda)=(\lambda^{(0)},\dots,\lambda^{(e-1)})$ and $e$-core
$C_e(\lambda)$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Then there is a
bijection $f$ from the set of hooks of $\lambda$ of $e$-divisible length onto
the set of hooks of the multipartition $Q_e(\lambda)$, that is, onto
$\bigsqcup_{i=0}^{e-1}\{\text{hooks of }\lambda^{(i)}\}$, such that
$$|H|=e\,|f(H)|\qquad\text{and}\qquad Q_e\bigl(\lambda\setminus H\bigr)=Q_e(\lambda)\setminus f(H),$$
where the right-hand side means that the hook $f(H)$ is removed from the single
component of $Q_e(\lambda)$ that contains it. On the $e$-abacus, $f$ is the
rescaling $b=b'e+i$, $g=g'e+i$ of a bead-gap pair $(b,g)$ lying on a common
runner $i$, followed by the bead-gap dictionary of the runner
([[lem-hooks-are-bead-gap-pairs-on-an-abacus]]).

Here and in the quotient components, removing a hook means deleting its
corresponding rim border strip as in
[[lem-hooks-are-bead-gap-pairs-on-an-abacus]](ii), rather than its arm-and-leg
node set.

No choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An integer $e\ge2$, a partition $\lambda\vdash n$, a normalised $\beta$-set $X=\{h_1>\cdots>h_m\}$ of $\lambda$, so that $e\mid m=|X|$, with runner label sets $X^{(e)}_i$, top-packed set $X^{(e)}$ and quotient components $\lambda^{(i)}=P(X^{(e)}_i)$ as in [[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]].

[F1] For a $\beta$-set $Y$ of a partition $\mu$ the hooks of $\mu$ correspond bijectively to the bead-gap pairs $(b,g)$ of $Y$, with $b\in Y$, $g\notin Y$ and $0\le g<b$, the hook of $(b,g)$ having length $b-g$; the hook has $e$-divisible length if and only if $b\equiv g\pmod e$; and removing the hook of $(b,g)$ replaces $Y$ by $(Y\setminus\{b\})\cup\{g\}$, a $\beta$-set for the partition $\mu$ with that hook removed ([[lem-hooks-are-bead-gap-pairs-on-an-abacus]]).

[F2] For $i\in\{0,\dots,e-1\}$ the runner label set $X^{(e)}_i$ is a $\beta$-set for the partition $\lambda^{(i)}=P(X^{(e)}_i)$, and position $ae+i$ of the abacus lies on runner $i$ at row $a$, so that the beads of $X^{(e)}_i$ are exactly the beads of $X$ on runner $i$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]], [[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]]).

[F3] The chosen $\beta$-set is normalised, $e\mid m$; the removal of a hook does not change the number of beads, so the new $\beta$-set remains normalised ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Write a hook $H=H_{i,j}(\lambda)$ of $e$-divisible length in its bead-gap form $(b,g)$ with $b\in X$, $g\notin X$, $0\le g<b$ and $h:=|H|=b-g$. By $e\mid h$ we have $b\equiv g\pmod e$; write the common residue as $s\in\{0,\dots,e-1\}$ and $$b=b'e+s,\qquad g=g'e+s,\qquad b'=\frac{b-s}{e}>g'=\frac{g-s}{e}\ge0.$$ The bead $b$ is a bead of $X$ on runner $s$ and the gap $g$ is a gap of $X$ on runner $s$. [F1, F2]

2.1 Applying step 1.1 conversely, a bead $b'\in X^{(e)}_s$ and a gap $g'\notin X^{(e)}_s$ with $0\le g'<b'$ give the bead-gap pair $(b,g)=(b'e+s,g'e+s)$ of $X$ with $e\mid(b-g)$ and $b-g=e(b'-g')$. Hence $f(H):=$ the hook of $\lambda^{(s)}$ attached to the bead-gap pair $(b',g')$ of the $\beta$-set $X^{(e)}_s$ is well defined, and $f$ is bijective onto the hooks of $\bigsqcup_i\lambda^{(i)}$ because both sides are in bijection with the bead-gap pairs of $X$ whose two positions share a runner, respectively with the union over $s$ of the bead-gap pairs of $X^{(e)}_s$; the length identity is $|H|=b-g=e(b'-g')=e|f(H)|$. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 For the removal identity, let $X'=(X\setminus\{b\})\cup\{g\}$ be the $\beta$-set of $\lambda\setminus H$ from [F1], again of size $m$ and hence normalised by [F3]. Because $b$ and $g$ lie on runner $s$, the beads of $X'$ on a runner $t\ne s$ are exactly the beads of $X$ on runner $t$, and the beads on runner $s$ have row labels $(X^{(e)}_s\setminus\{b'\})\cup\{g'\}$. Consequently, computing the quotient from the normalised sets by [F2], $$\lambda'^{(t)}=P\bigl((X')^{(e)}_t\bigr)=\lambda^{(t)}\ (t\ne s),\qquad \lambda'^{(s)}=P\bigl((X^{(e)}_s\setminus\{b'\})\cup\{g'\}\bigr),$$ and the last partition is $\lambda^{(s)}$ with its hook $f(H)$ removed, by [F1] applied to the $\beta$-set $X^{(e)}_s$ of $\lambda^{(s)}$. This is exactly the assertion $Q_e(\lambda\setminus H)=Q_e(\lambda)\setminus f(H)$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Steps 2.1 and 3.1 together exhibit the required bijection $f$ with the length and removal identities, and the description of $f$ on the abacus is the rescaling of step 1.1 followed by the bead-gap dictionary of the runner in step 2.1. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

items.title: The core-quotient size formula defines the weight
items.statement:
Let $e\ge2$ and let $\lambda\vdash n$ with $e$-core $C_e(\lambda)$ and
$e$-weight $w_e(\lambda)=|Q_e(\lambda)|$
([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Then
$$n=|\lambda|=|C_e(\lambda)|+e\,w_e(\lambda),$$
so $w_e(\lambda)=(n-|C_e(\lambda)|)/e\in\mathbb N_0$. Equivalently every
sequence of removals of removable border strips of size $e$ from $\lambda$ down
to its $e$-core
([[thm-e-core-is-independent-of-the-rim-hook-removal-order]]) has exactly
$w_e(\lambda)$ steps, and $w_e(\lambda)=|Q_e(\lambda)|$ equals both the number
of hooks of the multipartition $Q_e(\lambda)$ and, by the bijection of
[[thm-e-quotient-controls-hooks-divisible-by-e]], the number of hooks of
$\lambda$ of length divisible by $e$.

Throughout the proof, $\lambda\setminus H$ means deletion of the rim strip
corresponding to the node hook $H$, as in
[[thm-e-quotient-controls-hooks-divisible-by-e]].

No choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An integer $e\ge2$ and a partition $\lambda\vdash n$ with $e$-quotient $Q_e(\lambda)=(\lambda^{(0)},\dots,\lambda^{(e-1)})$, $e$-core $C_e(\lambda)$ and $e$-weight $w_e(\lambda)=\sum_i|\lambda^{(i)}|$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]).

[F1] $C_e(\lambda)$ is well defined and is the terminal partition of every maximal sequence of removals of removable border strips of size $e$ from $\lambda$; each removed strip has size exactly $e$ and the terminal partition contains no hook of length $e$ ([[thm-e-core-is-independent-of-the-rim-hook-removal-order]]).

[F2] There is a bijection $f$ from the hooks of $\lambda$ of $e$-divisible length onto the hooks of the multipartition $Q_e(\lambda)$ with $|H|=e\,|f(H)|$ and $Q_e(\lambda\setminus H)=Q_e(\lambda)\setminus f(H)$, where the latter removes the hook $f(H)$ from its component ([[thm-e-quotient-controls-hooks-divisible-by-e]]).

[F3] For a partition $\mu$, the number of hooks of $\mu$ equals $|\mu|$, since each box is the anchor of exactly one hook of $[\mu]$ ([[def-hook-arm-leg-and-hook-length]]); a nonempty partition has a removable box, that is, a hook of size $1$ ([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]); and a hook of the multipartition $Q_e(\lambda)$ has the size of the corresponding hook of the component $\lambda^{(i)}$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]], [[thm-e-quotient-controls-hooks-divisible-by-e]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** induction on $w_e(\lambda)$.

1.1 We first record the counting consequences of the quotient theorem. A hook of $\lambda$ has $e$-divisible length exactly when it is the preimage under the bijection $f$ of [F2] of a hook of $Q_e(\lambda)$, and the number of hooks of a partition equals its size by [F3]; hence the number of $e$-divisible hooks of $\lambda$ equals the total size $w_e(\lambda)=\sum_i|\lambda^{(i)}|$ of $Q_e(\lambda)$. In particular $Q_e(\lambda)$ has a hook if and only if $w_e(\lambda)>0$, and then some hook has size $1$ by [F3], so $\lambda$ has a hook of length $e$. [F2, F3]

2.1 Base case: if $w_e(\lambda)=0$ then $Q_e(\lambda)$ has no hook by step 1.1, so $\lambda$ has no hook of $e$-divisible length, hence no hook of length $e$; by [F1] the terminal partition of the empty removal sequence is $\lambda$ itself, that is, $C_e(\lambda)=\lambda$, and the removal sequence has $0=w_e(\lambda)$ steps. [F1, base, step 1.1]

2.2 Induction step: let $w_e(\lambda)>0$. By step 1.1 there is a hook $H$ of $\lambda$ of length exactly $e$, a removable border strip of size $e$ by [F1]. By the removal identity of [F2], $$Q_e(\lambda\setminus H)=Q_e(\lambda)\setminus f(H),$$ and since $f(H)$ is a hook of a component of $Q_e(\lambda)$ of size $|H|/e=1$, the right-hand side is the multipartition obtained by deleting one box, so by [F3] its size is $w_e(\lambda)-1$. Moreover $C_e(\lambda\setminus H)=C_e(\lambda)$: a maximal sequence from $\lambda\setminus H$ is the tail of a maximal sequence from $\lambda$ beginning with $H$, and all maximal sequences from $\lambda$ end at $C_e(\lambda)$ by [F1]. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 By step 2.2 we may apply the induction hypothesis to $\lambda\setminus H$, whose weight is $w_e(\lambda)-1<w_e(\lambda)$: every maximal sequence of $e$-strip removals from $\lambda\setminus H$ has $w_e(\lambda)-1$ steps and $$|\lambda|-e=|\lambda\setminus H|=|C_e(\lambda\setminus H)|+e\,(w_e(\lambda)-1)=|C_e(\lambda)|+e\,w_e(\lambda)-e,$$ so $|\lambda|=|C_e(\lambda)|+e\,w_e(\lambda)$; and appending the single step $H$ shows that every maximal sequence from $\lambda$ has exactly $w_e(\lambda)$ steps, because $H$ was an arbitrary possible first $e$-hook removal and step 2.2 applies to every such first step. [F1, IH, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 The base case of step 2.1 and the induction step of steps 2.2 and 3.1 establish the size formula and the step count for every partition of finite weight, and the counting statement is step 1.1. This is all that was asserted. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, discharge-induction: step 2.2] ∎

items.title: q-Schur Weyl modules are in the same block iff their labels have the same e-core
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with quantum characteristic $e$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]], [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]]), let $n\ge0$ and $d\ge n$, and let $W^{\lambda}_F$ be the Weyl modules of $S_F(d,n)$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). Then for partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ with at most $d$ parts, $W^{\lambda}_F$ and $W^{\mu}_F$ lie in the same block of $S_F(d,n)$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $e$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Consequently, for finite $e$, the blocks of $S_F(d,n)$ are indexed by the $e$-cores $\gamma$ with $|\gamma|\le n$ and $|\gamma|\equiv n\pmod e$, and the block of $W^{\lambda}_F$ is determined by $C_e(\lambda)$. For $e=\infty$ we set $C_\infty(\lambda):=\lambda$; the algebra is semisimple and its blocks are indexed by the partitions of $n$.

No choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A field $F$, parameter $q$, quantum characteristic $e$, integer $d\ge n$, and the Weyl modules in the statement. Write $S=S_F(d,n)$ and $W^{\lambda}=W^{\lambda}_F$.

[F1] The semistandard cellular basis has cells $W^{\lambda}$, nonzero absolutely simple heads $L^{\lambda}$, and dominance-unitriangular decomposition multiplicities $d_{\lambda\mu}$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). The cellular anti-involution induces contragredient duality fixing the simple isomorphism classes, through the nondegenerate cell form on each simple head ([[lem-cell-form-is-associative-and-its-radical-is-a-submodule]], [[thm-nonzero-cell-heads-classify-the-simple-modules-of-a-cellular-algebra]]).

[F2] The balanced hook-ratio Jantzen formula and alternating beta symbols ([[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]], [[def-alternating-weyl-and-specht-symbols-from-beta-sequences]]) use conjugate beta numbers $\beta_j=\lambda'_j+N-j$, with $N$ sufficiently large, and read $$\sum_{r>0}[W^{\lambda}(r)]=\sum_{(a,b),(a,c)\in[\lambda],\ b<c}\bigl(v(h^{\lambda}_{ab})-v(h^{\lambda}_{ac})\bigr)[W^{\beta+h^{\lambda}_{ac}\varepsilon_b-h^{\lambda}_{ac}\varepsilon_c}],$$ where $W^{\lambda}(r)$ are filtration submodules, $W^{\lambda}(1)=\operatorname{rad}W^{\lambda}$, and the right hand symbols are zero on repeated or negative entries and otherwise have the sign of sorting the beta sequence. The suppliers must carry this balanced form; the earlier displayed unbalanced manuscript indices do not preserve degree.

[F3] Core abaci are obtained by packing beads upwards on each runner, so their shapes depend only on runner bead counts; rim-hook removal is a bead-to-gap move ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]], [[thm-e-core-is-independent-of-the-rim-hook-removal-order]], [[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]]). Conjugation reverses dominance ([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]). Transposing every strip in a maximal $e$-hook removal sequence gives such a sequence for the conjugate partition; hook lengths are preserved by transposition, so its terminal core is the conjugate core. Hence $C_e(\lambda')=C_e(\lambda)'$.

[F4] Primitive central idempotents decompose the identity, and every finite-dimensional module splits into their block summands ([[def-blocks-of-a-finite-dimensional-algebra-by-primitive-central-idempotents]]). Weyl classes are linearly independent in the Grothendieck group, so a nonzero accumulated Weyl coefficient in the class of a module supported in one block forces that Weyl module into the block ([[lem-virtual-weyl-combinations-detect-q-schur-block-separation]], [[lem-semistandard-weight-dimensions-detect-virtual-weyl-classes]]).



[F5] The radical of a finite-dimensional algebra is nilpotent and its quotient semisimple ([[thm-jacobson-radical-is-nilpotent-and-the-quotient-is-semisimple]]); the Wedderburn decomposition is a product of matrix rings over division rings ([[thm-wedderburn-artin-theorem]]). Cellular ideal layers are the tensor products of the contragredient left cell and the right cell ([[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Lift and valuation. Use $R=F[X]_{(X-q)}$ with $\hat q=X$ and uniformizer $X-q$. The element $X$ is a unit since $q\ne0$, and every polynomial $[m]_X=1+X+\cdots+X^{m-1}$ is nonzero, so the generic factorial is nonzero. For $n=0$, $S_F(d,0)=F$, with its one empty-label module, so all assertions hold directly; hence assume $n>0$. Its valuation $v(m)$ is positive exactly when $[m]_q=0$, equivalently $e\mid m$ for finite $e$; for $e=\infty$ all valuations vanish. In characteristic $p$ the positive valuation may exceed1, which causes no difficulty below. [given, F2, algebra]

1.2 Block support and Jantzen edges. A finite-dimensional module with simple head is indecomposable: every nonzero summand has nonzero head, so two summands would make the head nonsimple. Thus $W^{\lambda}$ has just one nonzero block summand, and every Jantzen submodule is supported in that block. By [F4], any nonzero accumulated coefficient $J_{\lambda\mu}$ of $[W^{\mu}]$ in [F2] puts $W^{\lambda},W^{\mu}$ in the same block. This uses the sum of submodule classes, without identifying it with the radical class. [F1, F2, F4]

2.1 Balanced terms preserve the core and descend in dominance. Put $s=h_{ab}$ and $t=h_{ac}$, so $s-t=\beta_b-\beta_c$. If a hook coefficient is nonzero, at least one of $s,t$ is divisible by $e$. If $e\mid t$, the shifted bead residues are unchanged. Otherwise $e\mid s$, so $t\equiv\beta_c-\beta_b\pmod e$ and the two shifted residues exchange. Thus every surviving symbol has the same runner counts and core as $\lambda$. Moreover replacing the two conjugate beta entries $u>v$ by $u+t,v-t$ strictly increases conjugate majorization; the sorted target therefore strictly decreases original dominance. Accumulating equal target labels preserves both conclusions. [F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 No outgoing edge implies a binary row condition. Suppose every accumulated outgoing coefficient from $\mu$ is zero. For row $i$, put $g_i=N+i-1-\mu_i$, a gap in its conjugate beta set; its row hooks are exactly $\beta_j-g_i>0$. If that row contained a divisible hook $s$ and a nondivisible hook $t$, repeatedly replace $t$ by $s+t$ while their sum is another row hook. This finite climb ends with $s+t$ absent from the hook set. The balanced term for the nodes of hook lengths $s,t$ then has lower shifted bead $g_i$, which is a gap, and upper shifted bead $g_i+s+t$, which is absent from the beta set. Its symbol survives and its coefficient is $\pm v(s)\ne0$. There is no cancellation: any surviving balanced term replaces two lost values by a new value larger than both and a new value smaller than both, so those four values determine the pair and its row gap uniquely; the gaps $g_i$ strictly increase with $i$. This contradicts the zero accumulated coefficient. Therefore each row has either all hook lengths divisible by $e$ or none; call this the binary row condition. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Composition-factor cores. An off-head simple occurs in $W^{\lambda}$ exactly when it occurs in its radical, equivalently in the positive Jantzen sum: the first submodule is the radical and every later one is contained in it. Its nonzero multiplicity in that sum implies it occurs in some $W^{\mu}$ with $J_{\lambda\mu}\ne0$, since otherwise its coefficient in the sum would be zero. Step 2.1 gives the same core and strict dominance descent. Induction on the finite dominance poset proves that every factor $L^{\nu}$ of $W^{\lambda}$ has $C_e(\nu)=C_e(\lambda)$. No identity equating the radical class with the positive sum is asserted. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 Vertical core removal under the binary row condition. A removable $e$-hook has hook length $e$ at its defining node. Every hook in that row is then divisible, so its last-column hook, a positive multiple of $e$ no larger than $e$, equals $e$. Hook lengths strictly decrease across the row, forcing the defining node to be at the row end: the strip is vertical on $e$ equal-length rows $i,\ldots,i+e-1$ in column $j$. Removing it decreases that column height by $e$. In unaffected rows hook divisibility is unchanged. For an affected row $i+t$, hooks in the retained columns were all congruent to $-t$ modulo $e$, because row $i$ had all hooks divisible and those rows had equal length. Their new hook lengths are all congruent to $-t-1$, so the binary row condition persists. Induction shows every core-removal strip is vertical. [F3, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 The Cartan graph locally. Choose a complete orthogonal primitive idempotent system of $S$, with one representative $f_\mu$ for each simple label and repeated representatives as necessary. By [F5] and the absolute simplicity in [F1], the semisimple quotient is a product of full matrix rings over $F$. Lift its matrix diagonal idempotents: the radical is nilpotent and the iteration $u\mapsto u+(1-2u)(u^2-u)$ changes an error $a=u^2-u$ to $-3a^2+4a^3$, so finite iteration lifts an idempotent; successively working in complementary corners lifts an orthogonal system. Absolute simplicity gives $\dim L^{\lambda}f_\mu=\delta_{\lambda\mu}$, hence exact multiplication by $f_\mu$ gives $\dim W^{\lambda}f_\mu=d_{\lambda\mu}$. The successive cellular ideal bimodules are the contragredient cell module tensor the right cell module. Apply the exact projection $f_\mu(-)f_\nu$ and add their dimensions; [F1]'s duality fixes the simple labels, giving $\dim f_\mu Sf_\nu=\sum_\lambda d_{\lambda\mu}d_{\lambda\nu}$. This is the Cartan entry of the primitive projective $f_\mu S$. A disconnected graph on the full primitive idempotent system, with edges whenever either mixed corner is nonzero, yields central idempotents by summing each component: all mixed corners vanish in both directions. Conversely a central block idempotent forbids mixed corners. Thus simple labels in one block are joined by pairs sharing a Weyl factor, and step 3.1 proves that labels in the same block have the same core. [F1, F4, F5, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 The minimum label and the bridge shapes. Assume $e<\infty$. Fix core $\gamma$ and weight $w$, with $l=\ell(\gamma)$, and set $\rho=(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_l,1^{ew})$. It has core $\gamma$ by removing its bottom vertical $e$-strips, and is dominance-minimal in the class: every same-core partition contains $\gamma$ as a diagram, and appending all additional boxes as rows of size1 minimizes each dominance partial sum. Let $\mu\ne\rho$ satisfy the binary row condition. Choose the first row $i$ with divisible hooks and put $j=\mu_i$, $h=h^{\mu}_{ij}=\mu'_j-i+1$, a positive multiple of $e$. If $j=1$, every divisible hook is in column1, so step 3.2 would give $\mu=\rho$; thus $j>1$. Remove the vertical $h$-strip, obtaining $\sigma$, then add $h$ boxes horizontally to its first row to get $\nu$, and vertically to its first column to get $\eta$. All have the same core, since $h$ is a multiple of $e$; $\nu$ dominates $\mu,\eta$, and $\eta$ is strictly below $\mu$ because the removed nodes are moved into new bottom rows. [F3, step 3.2, construct, algebra]

5.1 The bridge coefficients are nonzero. Write $l=\ell(\mu)=\ell(\sigma)$. If $i>1$, then $\sigma_1=\mu_1$ and the row1 hook pair in $\nu$ at columns $j,\mu_1+1$ has lengths $A=h^{\mu}_{1j}$ and $h$: the first is nondivisible because row1 precedes the first divisible row, and the second is divisible. Its balanced symbol sorts to $\mu$, so its coefficient is nonzero. If $i=1$, then $\sigma_1=j-1$, and the row1 pair at columns $j,j+1$ has lengths $h,h-1$; its balanced transfer $h-1$ sorts to $\mu$, again giving a nonzero coefficient. For $\eta$, the pair at columns $1,\sigma_1+1$ has lengths $A'=\sigma_1+h+l-1$ and $h$. When $i>1$, $A'-h^{\mu}_{i1}=A$, so $A'$ is nondivisible; when $i=1$, $A'=h^{\mu}_{11}+h-1$, also nondivisible. Its balanced symbol sorts to $\eta$. Each claimed target has precisely two lost and two gained beta values, so the uniqueness argument in step 2.2 rules out cancellation. Thus both $J_{\nu\mu}$ and $J_{\nu\eta}$ are nonzero. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.2, step 4.2, algebra]

6.1 Connectivity and sufficiency. Induct upwards from $\rho$ in the finite dominance poset. For $\mu\ne\rho$, if an outgoing coefficient $J_{\mu\tau}$ is nonzero, then $\tau$ is strictly below $\mu$ in the same core class by step 2.1, so induction connects $\tau$, and hence $\mu$, to $\rho$. If no outgoing coefficient exists, steps 2.2, 3.2, 4.2 and 5.1 connect $\mu$ to $\nu$ and then $\eta$, with $\eta$ strictly below $\mu$, and induction again connects it to $\rho$. Every such edge is a same-block implication by step 1.2. Thus every pair of labels of the same core lies in the same block. Together with step 4.1 this proves the equivalence. [step 1.2, step 2.1, step 4.1, step 2.2, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Parameterization and infinite characteristic. Every simple is the head of a Weyl module, so every block has a partition label. The core sizes are $n-ew$, and each admissible core occurs via the partition $\rho$ of step 4.2; step 6.1 therefore gives the stated indexing. If $e=\infty$, all coefficients vanish by step 1.1, so positivity forces every first Jantzen submodule, hence every radical, to vanish. All Weyl modules are simple; their decomposition matrix is the identity. Step 4.1 then gives identity Cartan matrix, so every primitive projective is simple and $S$ is semisimple, with each partition its own block and core. This proves all assertions. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 4.1, step 4.2, step 6.1] ∎

items.title: The weight-one block decomposition pattern
items.statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with finite quantum characteristic $2\le e<\infty$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), let $\gamma$ be an $e$-core of $m$, put $n=m+e$, and fix $d\ge n$ ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). There are exactly $e$ partitions $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_e$ of $n$ with $e$-core $\gamma$; list them in dominance order, $\lambda_1\rhd\lambda_2\rhd\cdots\rhd\lambda_e$. In the source's (Murphy) normalisation the Weyl modules and simple modules of this weight-one class satisfy $W^{\lambda_e}=L^{\lambda_e}$ and $$[W^{\lambda_k}]=[L^{\lambda_k}]+[L^{\lambda_{k+1}}]\qquad(1\le k<e),$$ so the decomposition matrix of the class is the $e\times e$ bidiagonal matrix with rows and columns $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_e$. Moreover exactly $\lambda_1$ is not $e$-restricted, while $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_e$ are. Under the Schur functor ([[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]]) the corresponding Murphy Specht classes are $$[S^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_2}_{\mathrm M}],\qquad [S^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}]+[D^{\lambda_{k+1}}_{\mathrm M}]\ (2\le k<e),\qquad [S^{\lambda_e}_{\mathrm M}]=[D^{\lambda_e}_{\mathrm M}],$$ with $D^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}=0$; conjugating partitions and applying the same $\theta$ pullback to both modules ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]], [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]) gives the corresponding decomposition matrix for the page's Dipper-James Specht modules in $e$-regular labels.

No choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A field $F$, $q\in F^{\times}$ with finite quantum characteristic $2\le e<\infty$, an $e$-core $\gamma$ of $m$, the integer $n=m+e$, and the Weyl modules $W^{\lambda}_F$ of $S_F(d,n)$ for $\lambda\vdash n$ with at most $d$ parts, where $d\ge n$.

[F1] Each Weyl module has simple head $L^{\lambda}$ of multiplicity one, the decomposition matrix is dominance-unitriangular, and all simple modules are obtained this way ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). In a finite-dimensional module, a simple head implies indecomposability: any nonzero direct summand has a nonzero head, so two nonzero summands would give a nonsimple head.

[F2] The corrected balanced Jantzen formula sums positive filtration **submodules**, not their successive quotients: $$\sum_{i>0}[W^{\lambda}_F(i)]=\sum_{(a,b),(a,c)\in[\lambda],\ b<c}\bigl(\nu_\pi([h^{\lambda}_{ab}]_{\hat q})-\nu_\pi([h^{\lambda}_{ac}]_{\hat q})\bigr)[W^{\beta+h^{\lambda}_{ac}\varepsilon_b-h^{\lambda}_{ac}\varepsilon_c}_F].$$ Here $\beta_b=\lambda'_b+N-b$ for a fixed sufficiently long conjugate beta sequence, and the right hand symbols are alternating symbols: sort strictly decreasing, attach the sorting sign, and vanish on repeated or negative entries. The equal transfer preserves total size. Moreover $W(1)=\operatorname{rad}W$. This is the balanced hook-ratio formula required from [[thm-q-schaper-virtual-radical-layer-formula]] and [[def-alternating-weyl-and-specht-symbols-from-beta-sequences]]. Its source arithmetic must be repaired before binding: the manuscript's displayed beta indices are inconsistent, while its worked Example 5.28 determines the balanced transfer.

[F3] Core-quotient and abacus theory: a weight-one partition is obtained from a packed core abacus by moving the bottom bead of one runner down one place. The bead move removes/adds a rim $e$-hook, and distinct runners give distinct partitions ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]], [[thm-e-core-is-independent-of-the-rim-hook-removal-order]], [[def-beta-set-and-e-runner-abacus-of-a-partition]]). Restricted means $\lambda_i-\lambda_{i+1}<e$ for every $i$ ([[def-e-regular-and-e-restricted-partitions]]).

[F4] The exact Schur functor sends $W^{\lambda}$ to $S^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$ and $L^{\lambda}$ to $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$, whose nonzero labels are precisely the restricted partitions. The ordinary Specht dictionary is the proved generic-$q$ form bridge and uses conjugation and the same $\theta$ pullback on every module ([[def-schur-idempotent-and-schur-functor-for-type-a-q-schur-algebras]], [[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]], [[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]], [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Enumeration and ordering. Choose a conjugate core beta set long enough that every runner contains a bead, and list its bottom beads $x_1<\cdots<x_e$. Take this beta length divisible by $e$. Every partition with this core has, at the same beta length, the same packed set: its packed set represents $\gamma$ and the length uniquely determines a beta-set for $\gamma$. Weight one means its total runner displacement from packing is one, so exactly one bottom bead moves down one row. Conversely each such move adds exactly $e$ boxes and preserves the core. Thus replacing $x_k$ by $x_k+e$ gives precisely the $e$ weight-one partitions, denoted $\lambda_k$. For $j>k$, moving $x_j$ instead of $x_k$ gives the more dominant conjugate partition: the two bead lists differ by replacing $x_k+e,x_j$ with $x_k,x_j+e$. The new maximum is larger than both old values and the new minimum smaller than both, with the same sum. For each number of selected entries, the largest possible sum therefore does not decrease, and at least one sorted prefix increases. The sorted conjugate parts differ from these prefixes by the same beta offsets. Conjugation reverses dominance, hence $\lambda_1\rhd\cdots\rhd\lambda_e$. For the empty core put $\gamma_i=0$. The largest original partition is $(\gamma_1+e,\gamma_2,\ldots)$, since its added horizontal first-row strip dominates every other placement. [F3, construct, algebra]

1.2 Choose a lift with valuation one. If $q\ne1$, its finite quantum characteristic $e$ is its multiplicative order, and is prime to the field characteristic; use $R=F[X]_{(X-q)}$ and $\hat q=X$. The derivative of $X^e-1$ at $q$ is $eq^{e-1}\ne0$, so $\nu([e]_X)=1$; also $\nu([h]_X)=0$ when $e\nmid h$. If $q=1$, then $\operatorname{char}F=p=e$. First work over $\mathbb F_p$ with $R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}$, $\hat q=1$, giving $\nu([e]_1)=\nu(p)=1$ and $\nu([h]_1)=0$ for $p\nmid h$, and then extend scalars to $F$. This extension preserves the decomposition multiplicities because the q-Schur simple modules are absolutely irreducible and its integral Weyl modules commute with scalar extension. In both cases the generic factorial is nonzero and [F2] applies. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 Restriction. If $\lambda$ is not restricted, some $\lambda_i-\lambda_{i+1}\ge e$, so removing the last $e$ boxes of row $i$ leaves a partition. Its size is $|\gamma|$ and its core is $\gamma$, so it equals $\gamma$. Thus $\lambda$ is obtained by adding $e$ boxes to row $i$ of $\gamma$. An $e$-core has $\gamma_r-\gamma_{r+1}<e$ for every $r$, since otherwise it has a removable horizontal $e$-strip. Consequently $i>1$ is impossible: the partition inequality $\gamma_{i-1}\ge\gamma_i+e$ would contradict this core property. Therefore the only nonrestricted member is $\lambda_1=(\gamma_1+e,\gamma_2,\ldots)$; it is indeed nonrestricted because its first-row difference is at least $e$. [F3, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Evaluate the balanced formula. A nonzero coefficient involves a hook of length divisible by $e$. A weight-one abacus has exactly one bead-gap pair of equal residue with the gap below the bead: $x_k+e$ and $x_k$; thus its only $e$-divisible hook has length $e$. Any surviving term in [F2] replaces two bead values, and its new runner counts equal the old ones: either $e$ divides the transfer $h_{ac}$, leaving residues fixed, or $e$ divides $h_{ab}=h_{ac}+\beta_b-\beta_c$, exchanging their residues. Hence its sorted symbol is one of the $\lambda_j$. For $j>k$, the distinct bead sets of $\lambda_k$ and $\lambda_j$ differ exactly by replacing $x_k+e,x_j$ with $x_k,x_j+e$. There is exactly one balanced transfer yielding this change: if $x_j<x_k+e$, its two hook lengths are $h_{ab}=e$, $h_{ac}=x_j-x_k$; if $x_j>x_k+e$, they are $h_{ab}=x_j-x_k$, $h_{ac}=e$. The difference $x_j-x_k$ is not divisible by $e$ since bottom beads are on distinct runners. Thus the respective unsigned coefficients are $+1$ and $-1$ by step 1.2. Sorting gives in either case the signed coefficient $(-1)^{j-k+1}$: in the packed core set, exactly one bead from each runner with bottom bead $>x_r$ lies between $x_r$ and $x_r+e$, so moving $x_r$ crosses $e-r$ beads; the relative sorting parity for the two moves, together with their opposite orientation, is $(-1)^{(e-j)-(e-k)+1}$. There are no other terms and no repeated contributions: the two lost and two gained bead values determine the pair and transfer uniquely. Therefore $\sum_{i>0}[W^{\lambda_k}(i)]=\sum_{j>k}(-1)^{j-k+1}[W^{\lambda_j}]$. [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Descending induction and the matrix. For $k=e$, step 2.2 gives zero on the left; all summands are actual submodule classes with nonnegative simple multiplicities, so $W^{\lambda_e}(1)=0$ and $W^{\lambda_e}=L^{\lambda_e}$. Suppose the stated rows are known for $j>k$. Substitution into step 2.2 telescopes to $\sum_{i>0}[W^{\lambda_k}(i)]=[L^{\lambda_{k+1}}]$. Since $W(1)=\operatorname{rad}W$ and each later term is a submodule of $W(1)$, positivity shows $W(1)\cong L^{\lambda_{k+1}}$ and $W(i)=0$ for $i\ge2$. The head quotient is $L^{\lambda_k}$, giving $[W^{\lambda_k}]=[L^{\lambda_k}]+[L^{\lambda_{k+1}}]$. Notice that the identity $[W]=[L]+\sum_{i>0}[W(i)]$ is used only after proving all later filtration submodules vanish; it is false for a general Jantzen filtration. Reading simple multiplicities yields the complete $e\times e$ bidiagonal matrix. [F1, F2, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 Specht rows. Apply the exact functor of [F4] to step 3.1 and use step 2.1: $D^{\lambda_1}_{\mathrm M}=0$, while the other $D^{\lambda_k}_{\mathrm M}$ are the nonzero simples. This gives exactly the three displayed Murphy Specht class identities, hence the full $e\times(e-1)$ Murphy matrix. Conjugation sends the core to $\gamma'$ and the restricted simple labels to regular ones, and the same $\theta$ pullback applied to every module preserves all composition multiplicities. Thus the ordinary Specht matrix has the same entries under the accepted conjugate/sign label dictionary. [F4, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎
